APPROVAL OF MINUTES
  EL MONTE CITY COUNCIL REGULAR MEETING
  OF AUGUST 16, 2022

MEETING JOINTLY AND REGULARLY WITH THE EL MONTE HOUSING AUTHORITY; EL
MONTE PUBLIC FINANCING AUTHORITY; EL MONTE WATER AUTHORITY; EL MONTE
PARKING AUTHORITY; SUCCESSOR AGENCY TO THE FORMER EL MONTE COMMUNITY
REDEVELOPMENT AGENCY; HOUSING SUCCESSOR AGENCY; AND, FROM TIME TO
TIME, SUCH OTHER BODIES OF THE CITY WHOSE MEMBERSHIP IS COMPOSED
EXCLUSIVELY OF THE MEMBERSHIP OF THE CITY COUNCIL

1.  CALL TO ORDER: 6:03 p.m.

2.  ROLL CALL FOR CITY COUNCIL AND AUTHORITY BODIES:

  Jessica Ancona, Mayor/Chair – absent
  Alma D. Puente, Mayor Pro Tem/Authority Member – present
  Martin R. Herrera, Councilmember/Authority Member – present
  Victoria Martinez Muela, Councilmember/Authority Member – present via zoom
  Dr. Maria Morales, Councilmember/Authority Member – present

3.  APPROVAL OF AGENDA:

  m) Councilmember Herrera
  s) Dr. Morales  5-0
  Items 4.3 and 4.5 have been pulled

4.  CLOSED SESSION:

  The City Council and the various legislative bodies whose membership is composed
  exclusively of the membership of the City Council will attempt to address and complete all
  Closed Session business between 6:00 p.m. and 7:00 p.m. If the City Council completes
  all Closed Session business prior to 7:00 p.m., the City Council will take a short recess
  and commence all Open Session proceedings promptly at 7:00 p.m. In the event the City
  Council is unable to address or complete all agendized Closed Session items by 7:00
  p.m., the City Council will hear all such remaining items toward the end of the meeting,
  immediately following Council Communications. Should any member of the public wish to
  address the City Council on any agendized Closed Session matter, the City Council shall
  allow such person to address the City Council on such matter(s) prior to going into Closed
  Session, provided that all persons wishing to address the Council on an agendized Closed
  Session matter shall (i) call-in or submit a speaker card in the manner prescribed on page
  1 of this agenda, above, prior to the City Council going into closed session; and (ii) be
  subject to a single speaker time allotment of three (3) continuous minutes total per
  speaker to address the City Council on any or all closed session items of business.

  Mayor Pro Tem Puente invited members of the public to address the City Council
  on Closed Session Items 4.1 and 4.2.

  Mayor Pro Tem Puente and the City Council recessed into Closed Session at
  approximately 6:05 p.m. Mayor Ancona joined the City Council in Closed Session
  at approximately 6:15 p.m. Mayor Ancona and the City Council reconvened from
  Closed Session at approximately 7:00 p.m.
  Assistant City Attorney Richard Padilla reported out of Closed Session with respect
  to Items 4.1 and 4.2.

  4.1  Closed Session Pursuant to Government Code Section 54956.9(d)(2) and
  54956.9(e)(2) – Conference with Legal Counsel to Discuss Facts and
  Circumstances Which May Create Exposure to Litigation – One (1) Matter.

  Update provided by legal counsel Lloyd Pilchen, feedback given by the City
  Council, but not final action taken.
   City Council Meeting Minutes of August 16, 2022

  4.2  Closed Session Pursuant to Government Code Section 54956.9(a), (d)(2) and
  (e)(1) – Conference with Legal Counsel Regarding Anticipated Litigation – One (1)
  Potential Case.

  Update provided by legal counsel Lloyd Pilchen, feedback given by the City
  Council, but not final action taken.

  4.3  Closed Session Pursuant to Government Code Section 54956.9(d)(2) and
  54956.9(e)(2) – Conference with Legal Counsel – Anticipated Litigation/Significant
  Exposure to Litigation – One (1) Matter.

  Item has been pulled.

  4.4  Closed Session Pursuant to Government Code Section 54956.9(d)(1) –
  Conference with Legal Counsel Regarding Existing Litigation – Flores-Huicochea
  and Calederon vs. City of El Monte, Erick Ramos and Rene Flores, USDC Case
  No. 2:22-cv-00350-SPG-KS.

  Item has been pulled.

  4.5  Closed Session Pursuant to Government Code Section 54957.6 – Conference with
  Labor Negotiators.

  Bargaining Units Subject to Negotiations: El Monte General Unit (SEIU Local
  721); El Monte General Mid-Management Unit (SEIU Local 721); El Monte Police
  Officers Association; El Monte Police Mid-Manager’s Association; and All
  Unrepresented Employees of City Executive Team.

  City’s Designated Negotiator: Alma K. Martinez, City Manager and John Nguyen,
  Human Resources/Risk Management Director.

  Update provided by Human Resources staff, feedback given by the City
  Council, but no final action taken.

  OPEN SESSION PROCEEDINGS

(Commencing at 7:00 p.m. or as soon thereafter as the City Council reconvene from Closed
Session/Short Recess).

8.  GENERAL PUBLIC COMMENT:

  This time has been set aside for members of the public to directly address the City Council
  on agendized items of business (other than those agendized as public hearing or closed
  session items) or on any other matter of interest to the speaker/caller that is within the
  subject matter jurisdiction of the City Council, the Housing Authority, the Financing
  Authority and/or the Water Authority (collectively, the “Council”). Each speaker/caller will
  be limited to a single allotment of three (3) continuous minutes total to address the Council
  on any or all matters covered by this section. As explained more specifically under the
  Public Hearing portion of this agenda, members of the public wishing to offer comment on
  items of business agendized under the Public Hearing portion of the agenda shall have a
  separate allotment of three (3) continuous minutes per speaker per public hearing item.
  Except as otherwise provided under the Brown Act (Gov. Code Section 54950 et seq.),
  the Council may not deliberate or take action upon any matter not listed on this posted
  agenda but may order that any such matter be placed on the agenda for a subsequent
  meeting. The Council may also direct staff to investigate certain matters for consideration

  2
   City Council Meeting Minutes of August 16, 2022

  at a future meeting. Persons wishing to address the Council on matters covered under
  General Public Comment shall call in or submit a speaker card in the manner prescribed
  on page 1 of this agenda, above, by or before the General Public Comment portion of the
  agenda is closed. The City Council shall be under no obligation to entertain comments
  from speakers/callers who submit cards or call in to speak on matters covered by the
  section after the General Public Comment portion of the agenda is closed.

  Steve Ramirez – Spoke about the notification he received about not being able to run for
  office. There is a lot that he can accomplish.

  Stephen Trumble – Pleasure to be able to attend the Back to School Night. Wednesday,
  August 24th at 4:00pm there will be a program called the danger of alcohol abuse focusing
  on ages 13 to 17.

  Mary Ann Powers – Spoke about the appointment to committees and it is up to the entire
  Council in allowing these things to go forward. The EM Committee has been waiting for
  two years to have a spot filled.

  Elena Vasquez – Would like to take a moment to acknowledge the original inhabitants of
  this land. Opposed the murals that are being proposed.

  Rebekka Ramsay – Also opposes the murals with the pioneer narrative do not represents
  the students. Opposes the murals being proposed.
  Cosme Jimenez – Made comments regarding the transparency at City Hall.

  Gabriel Ramirez – Presented a formal complaint to the City Manager and the City Council
  regarding his filing fee.

  Destiny Flores – Spoke about two (2) programs that the California Insurance Department
  is offering.

  Written Public Comment –

  Romeo Guzman – Opposes the murals being proposed

  Andy Aparicio – Opposes the murals being proposed.

  18A.  Mayor Ancona

  18A.1 Update and Request for Report on Flair Drive Big Rig Parking Lot.

  Requested information regarding the big rig parking lot on Flair Drive.

  Assistant City Manager Sal Mendez provided an update regarding this item. Both
  Public Works and Economic Development are working together on this matter.

  Is this a permitted parking lot. Is there a Conditional Use Permit for this property.

  Staff is reviewing to see if the use can be permitted as a temporary use or not.
  There is an open case on this property.

  Mayor would like a copy of what was submitted to the City by the property
  representative.

  10
   City Council Meeting Minutes of August 16, 2022

Staff provided an update regarding the Flair Park Area Study. Consultant hired by
the City has provided her findings. The item will be presented to the Planning
Commission and then it will be presented to the City Council.

18A.2 Discussion and Direction on Needs Assessment Report for El Monte Police
  Department Regarding Personnel, Vehicle, Technology and Equipment.

At the last City Council meeting the POA President came up and asked for several
things. There are needs that the Department has. Requested a report from the
staff regarding how many officers are being proposed to being hired, what
equipment, vehicles are also needed.

Acting Chief Fisher has agreed to work on the needs assessment and bring it back
to the City Council.

Direction given to bring this item back to the City Council.

18A.3 Discussion and Direction on Recognition of the Officers who Responded to
  the Active Shooter Incident in Arcadia Acknowledging Their Life Savings
  Efforts and Assistance.

The Mayor provided an update regarding the event that took place in Arcadia.
Would like to commend the bravery of the officers who responded to this.

Acting Chief Fisher explained that this is being worked on now by the Department.

18A.4 Update on Outreach to Increase Safety Measures for El Monte Business
  Owners to Address Smash and Grab Crimes.

Maybe at the next meeting staff can bring back a progress report on this issue.

Acting Chief Fisher provided a quick update on the current work being done by the
Police Department on this.

18A.5 Request to Revisit Item 14.3 from the August 2nd Meeting: Extension of
  Downtown Mural Program and Reallocation of Funds.

The community has expressed their concern and opposition to the murals that
were proposed at the August 2nd City Council meeting. Would like for this item to
go before the Arts in Public Places Commission.

There is a meeting set up on Monday for the Arts in Public Places. The Art in
Public Places is to provide input regarding the proposed murals.

Dr. Morales would like to know what the legal procedures are in regards to
revisiting this item. Would like legal to come back and provide a legal opinion
regarding revisiting this item.

Staff can meet with the artist and provide feedback given by the City Council and
the community.

Dr. Morales recommended that legal provide a legal opinion regarding what was
approved by the City Council previously.

Councilmember Martinez Muela requested that staff provide the entire City Council
a copy of the agreement that the City entered into in regards to this item.

Councilmember Herrera understood that the term of the agreement was going to
be extended and that the Arts in Public Places committee will provide their
feedback.

Thanked staff in regards to the Back to School Resources Fair.
